resources.name: IoTInspector
quotes: To this end, we utilize a crowdsourced dataset of IoT TLS traffic collected by IoT Inspector [23], consisting of 2,014 IoT devices of 286 models from 65 device vendors, across 721 users worldwide.
IoT Inspector is an open-source tool that crowdsourced the network traffic from 54,094 devices across 5,404 users worldwide [23].
references: Danny Yuxing Huang, Noah Apthorpe, Frank Li, Gunes Acar, and Nick Feamster. 2020. Iot inspector: Crowdsourcing labeled network traffic from smart home devices at scale. Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies (2020).
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors utilize a crowdsourced dataset collected by IoT Inspector and describe it as an open-source tool used for their measurements.

resources.name: Certificate Transparency
quotes: We queried each certificate in CT logs [30] to check its existence.
Our study highlights potential concerns in the TLS/PKI practice by IoT device vendors. We aim to raise visibility for these issues and motivate vendors to improve security practice.
references: Ben Laurie, Adam Langley, and Emilia Kasper. 2013. Certificate Transparency. RFC 6962. (June 2013). https://doi.org/10.17487/RFC6962
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors query CT logs to check for the existence of the leaf certificates they captured.
